paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in Ahaz. The passage says he doesn't do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God, and when trouble comes, he never turns to the LORD. He sends messengers to Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, and says, "I am your servant and your son." That's a king putting a title on himself that belongs somewhere else (2 Kings 16:2, 7).

Then look at what he pays. He takes silver and gold from the house of the LORD and sends it to Assyria as a gift. Later he builds a copy of the Damascus altar and puts it to work all day, morning AND evening, while the bronze altar that stood before the LORD gets moved to the side. I think Ahaz was trying to buy safety, and it cost him the very things that belonged to God (2 Kings 16:8, 14-15).

So here's the question for you, baker. When the pressure hits, who do you run to first? I've been in the back of a junk drawer, and I know how scary a tight spot feels. But Ahaz shows us that a fast fix from somewhere else can cost more than the trouble did. The better move is to go to the LORD first, and this story isn't over, so keep baking.
